subject: Juniper discovery recap — eval recommendations & prompt sample request
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Yu <samantha.yu@juniper.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@juniper.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Juniper discovery recap — eval recommendations & prompt sample request

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo and for walking us through Juniper's customer support flows — that context was super helpful. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope an initial eval: 

Key takeaways from today
- Primary use: multi-turn support summarization + suggested response generation for Tier 1 agents (short, accuracy-sensitive).
- Volume: ~2.1M messages/month, peak concurrency ~420 req/min.
- Safety/PII constraints: must remove account IDs, credit card fragments, and customer SSNs before any evaluation artifact leaves your environment.
- Success criteria: <8% hallucination on our hallucination eval, avg response latency <450ms p50, and end-to-end relevance 90%+ on a labeled subset.

What we (Redwood) will provide by EOW: 
1) Eval playbook + benchmark runner instructions (link below).
2) Recommended model shortlist and quantization profiles for your latency/throughput targets.
3) A lightweight prompt-sample template for you to fill with real examples and edge cases.

What we need from you by next Thu (26 Jul):
- A CSV of 100 representative prompts (user messages) and 20 edge-case examples where current automation fails (file: juniper_prompts_v1.csv). Please mark any prompts that contain PII.
- Your redaction guidance: what to strip vs preserve (account IDs can be hashed, but case notes should retain timestamps).
- Any regulatory constraints that require on-prem evaluation.

Relevant links: Redwood eval playbook — https://redwood.ai/eval-playbook
HubSpot deal record — https://hubspot.com/deal/JUN-2027-114

Attachments: I attached a one-page requirements workbook (juniper_requirements.xlsx) to capture the data fields we need.

Suggested immediate next step: 30-min sync tomorrow (Tue 7/20) to walk through the prompt template and confirm redaction rules. If that works, Marcus will run the initial data ingestion and Ben will draft the eval plan.

Thanks —
Irene

Thanks, Irene — this is great and aligns with our internal notes. We can get a first batch together. A few clarifications: 

- For PII, we can provide redacted and non-redacted pairs for 25 examples so you can verify differential behavior.
- We have a regulatory constraint for EU accounts only; Juniper’s default is US-hosted. We'll flag EU-specific traffic in the CSV.

Attached: juniper_prompts_v1.csv — initial 60 prompts + 10 labeled edge cases. We'll add the rest by the deadline.

Confirming 7/20 10:00am PT for the 30-min sync. 

Samantha Yu

samantha.yu@juniper.ai

Attachment: juniper_prompts_v1.csv (CSV, 70 rows)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Yu <samantha.yu@juniper.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Juniper discovery recap — eval recommendations & prompt sample request

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Samantha — nice batch. High-level recommendations for your use case (short summary so we have a working plan for tomorrow):

Model shortlist (initial):
- redwood-8b-fp16 — best balance of quality/latency for multi-turn support.
- redwood-2.7b-quant — lower-cost, might be suitable for non-customer-facing suggestions (internal triage).
- redwood-chat-70b (hosted) — if Juniper wants to run a pilot for highest-quality summaries on a small subset.

Recommended first-run evals (we'll run these using the playbook):
1) Relevance & helpfulness (labeled subset of 300 messages).
2) Hallucination detection (contradiction + fabricated facts tests).
3) Latency/cost projection using your volume profile.

Two practical asks for your CSVs/samples: 
- Tag each prompt with "expected_output" where possible. That accelerates automated eval scoring.
- Flag any prompt where a factual lookup is required (these usually cause regressions post-quantization).

I've attached our eval runner instructions (eval_runner_instructions.pdf) and a quick template for expected_output. For tomorrow, Marcus will cover redaction best-practices and Laura will propose a pilot timing and contract sketch (SOW estimate).

Action items assigned:
- Marcus Lin: lead on redaction guidance + ingestion checklist (marcus.lin@redwood.com).
- Laura Bennett: draft SOW estimate and pilot scope (laura.bennett@redwood.com).
- Samantha: complete CSV and mark PII/region tags.

If Juniper is comfortable, we can run the first relevance eval within 7 business days after we receive the full 100-sample set.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: eval_runner_instructions.pdf

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@juniper.ai>

Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Juniper discovery recap — eval recommendations & prompt sample request

All — thanks for the clear plan. Two quick items before tomorrow's call: 

1) On redaction: Juniper's legal wants a short checklist we can sign off on. Marcus — could you prepare a one-page redaction checklist that maps fields -> redaction approach (hash/strip/preserve)?
2) On regressions: can you include a simple change-control proposal showing how Redwood will detect and notify us of quality regressions post-deploy (thresholds + rollbacks)? A one-paragraph summary is fine.

We'll be on the 10:00am PT sync. Tom (I might hop off at 10:25).

Tom Reynolds
VP Engineering | Juniper Systems
tom.reynolds@juniper.ai
+1 206-555-0190
